object: Column drum, short inscription cut on its sunk and smoothed surface
site: Gebel Barkal, great temple of Amun (L): column immediately in front of the right-hand pylon tower, facing the passage (found by Breasted, 1906)
notes: Griffith: 'The style is archaic.' 'Arekete qêli is like Wêsh-qêl in 75/16; the former word occurs in Kar.' (qo(2)li joined across his superscript accordingly); for nsp?er 'n-m-k-e-r might be read' (his alternative type ωSʓʒR); the word di-m?-e(l) runs across Griffith's type-line break and he cites it ('see 64, 70'); tiselke: its t-i-se-l part 'is perhaps the' t-i-?-o 'of 121'; the closing numeral is Griffith's 'i.e., "12" (?), cf. 101/4' (two strokes and a hooked stroke), written 12.
